/vaft/develop/reference/process/cocos/.title: Process reference: cocos
/vaft/develop/reference/process/cocos/.body: This page is generated from the docstrings of vaft/process/cocos.py: 6 public functions. The category overview and notation come from the module docstring; every entry below is what vaft.process.describe("cocos.<name>") prints. Back to the process reference index. Overview vaft.data.cocos declares what each convention and each external code is. This module answers whether a given equilibrium is actually consistent with the convention it claims, which is the check that catches a mislabelled file before its signs propagate into derived quantities. Sauter & Medvedev 2013 Eq. 23 gives six relations that any equilibrium in a given COCOS must satisfy, in terms of the signs of the plasma current and the vacuum toroidal field: =============== ===================================== quantity required sign =============== ===================================== F sigma_B0 Phi_tor sigma_B0 psi_edge - sigma_Ip * sigma_Bp psi_axis dp/dpsi -sigma_Ip * sigma_Bp j_phi sigma_Ip q sigma_Ip * sigma_B0 * sigma_rhotheta =============== ===================================== The q relation is reported as a warning rather than an error: Sauter Sect. IV notes that codes frequently emit abs(q), so a mismatch there is common and is not on its own evidence of a wrong index. Only four of the six are checkable against vaft.data.equilibrium.EquilibriumData as it stands: it carries no toroidal current density and no toroidal flux, so j_phi and Phi_tor are always reported as unverifiable. They are listed here because they are part of Eq. 23 and become checkable if those fields are ever added, not because they are being tested today. Functions cocos_consistency_signs — Observed sign of each Sauter Eq. 23 quantity, or None where not determinable. cocos_field_scales — The two sign multipliers that carry an equilibrium from one COCOS to another. identify_convention — Candidate COCOS indices for an equilibrium, from its observable signs. identify_flux_exponent — Decide whether psi is stored in weber or weber per radian, from Ampere’s law. identify_flux_exponent_from_q — Decide weber versus weber per radian by rebuilding q on closed contours. validate_cocos — Check an equilibrium against the Sauter Eq. 23 relations for one COCOS index. cocos_consistency_signs cocos_consistency_signs(equilibrium) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Observed sign of each Sauter Eq. 23 quantity, or None where not determinable. Reads signs off the equilibrium as it stands. Nothing is compared against a convention here and nothing is converted; validate_cocos does the comparison and vaft.process.equilibrium.convert_cocos is the only transform in the package. ParameterTypeUnitDescription equilibriumEquilibriumData-The equilibrium to inspect. Missing fields yield None for the relations that need them rather than an error. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription dict of str to int or None-Keys f, q, j_phi, phi_tor, dpsi, pprime; each +1, -1, or None when the field is absent or all-zero. Processing steps. f, q, j_phi and phi_tor: the sign of the profile’s median, with a deadband so a numerically-zero profile reports None. dpsi: the sign of psi_boundary - psi_axis. pprime: the stored pprime profile’s sign when the equilibrium carries one, which for a GEQDSK or an ODS it essentially always does. Only when it does not is the bulk slope (p_edge - p_axis)/(psi_edge - psi_axis) used instead, taken on a profile reordered axis-to-edge so the direction is known. Convention. Signs only, in whatever convention the equilibrium is already in; this function neither assumes nor imposes a COCOS. j_phi and phi_tor are always None today because vaft.data.equilibrium.EquilibriumData carries neither a toroidal current density nor a toroidal flux; they are reported so that Eq. 23 is represented in full, not because they are tested. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. A bulk slope is the sign of the overall trend, not of every point: a non-monotonic pressure profile still reports one sign. Because the stored pprime takes precedence, the fallback rarely runs in practice; that the two paths can disagree for a hand-built equilibrium is tracked in #605. Provenance. Sauter and Medvedev, Tokamak Coordinate Conventions: COCOS, Comput. Phys. Commun. 184, 293 (2013), Eq. 23, which defines the six sign relations this function measures. The preference for a bulk pressure slope over a pointwise derivative is that paper’s own recommendation. cocos_field_scales cocos_field_scales(source, target) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. The two sign multipliers that carry an equilibrium from one COCOS to another. ParameterTypeUnitDescription sourceint-The index the equilibrium is in. targetint-The index it is wanted in. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription tuple of int-(psi_scale, field_scale), each +1 or -1. psi_scale multiplies the poloidal flux – psi on the grid and the axis and boundary values with it – and field_scale multiplies the toroidal field and the poloidal current function F. Raises. ValueError Either index is not one of the eighteen COCOS indices. Processing steps. Look up both conventions’ sigma_Bp and sigma_RphiZ. The flux multiplier is the product of the two sigma_Bp sigma_RphiZ products; the field multiplier is the product of the two sigma_RphiZ. Convention. From Sauter Eq. 12, B_pol = sigma_Bp sigma_RphiZ grad(psi) x grad(phi) / (2 pi)**e_Bp: the sign psi carries relative to the physical poloidal field is the product sigma_Bp * sigma_RphiZ, so the flux flips when that product differs between the two conventions. The toroidal field’s direction follows sigma_RphiZ alone, so F and B_t flip when the handedness of (R, phi, Z) differs. This is a sign conversion, not a unit conversion. e_Bp differs between the 1-8 and 11-18 families by a factor of 2 pi on psi, and nothing here applies it: a caller crossing the families has to scale the flux itself, and identify_flux_exponent is what tells it which family a file is in. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Says nothing about sigma_rhothetaphi, which sets the poloidal angle’s direction. Two conventions differing only in that give (+1, +1) here and still disagree about the sign of theta – a caller relabelling a poloidal angle needs the third sigma, not these two. Provenance. O. Sauter and S. Yu. Medvedev, Comput. Phys. Commun. 184 (2013) 293, Eq. 12 and Table I. Two conversions measured on real runs, both reproduced by this rule: a COCOS 5 g-file into FLARE’s COCOS 3 needs (-1, +1), and a COCOS 2 CHEASE equilibrium needs (+1, -1). identify_convention identify_convention(equilibrium, *, clockwise_phi=None) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Candidate COCOS indices for an equilibrium, from its observable signs. Narrows rather than decides: the return is every index consistent with what the data shows, which is often more than one. A caller that needs a single index supplies the missing fact instead of guessing. ParameterTypeUnitDescription equilibriumEquilibriumData-Must carry bt0, ip, q and psi_1d; without them the candidate set is empty. clockwise_phibool, optional-Whether the machine’s toroidal angle runs clockwise seen from above. A fact about the machine, not about the data; without it both the odd and the even index of each pair are returned. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription tuple of int-The candidate COCOS indices in increasing order, empty when the required fields are missing or the sign identification fails. Processing steps. Reorder psi_1d and q axis-to-edge when the stored profile runs the other way. Get the sign family from omas.identify_cocos, which reads it off the signs of ip, bt0, q and the psi gradient. Narrow to 1-8 or 11-18 using identify_flux_exponent, falling back to identify_flux_exponent_from_q when that one had no inputs to measure, and keeping the full set when neither answers. Convention. Returns indices in the standard 1 to 18 numbering; 9 and 10 do not exist. The sign family and the storage family are identified by different evidence, signs for the first and an Ampere loop integral for the second, and either can be inconclusive on its own. What each index means is declared in vaft.data.cocos, not here. Applicability. Machine-independent. clockwise_phi is where a machine’s own geometry enters. Limitations. The axis-to-edge reorder exists because identify_cocos reads the psi gradient at the first node, so a boundary-first profile would invert the poloidal-flux sign silently. When both flux-exponent rungs abstain the result spans both storage families, and a caller that then converts must not assume the candidates share one. The contour-q rung is deliberately not consulted when the Ampere rung ran and rejected both families: that is a file whose ip and psi map disagree, and reporting a confident index for it would hide the disagreement rather than resolve it. Any exception from the underlying identification is reported as no candidates rather than raised. Provenance. Sauter and Medvedev (2013) for the index numbering and the sign relations the identification rests on. omas.identify_cocos supplies the sign family; its flux-exponent argument is deliberately not used, see identify_flux_exponent. The contour-q fallback is hsyun_GPEC library/geqdsk_cocos.py::flux_normalization_diagnostic, ported in identify_flux_exponent_from_q. identify_flux_exponent identify_flux_exponent(equilibrium) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Decide whether psi is stored in weber or weber per radian, from Ampere’s law. The loop integral of the poloidal field around the last closed flux surface equals mu0*|Ip|. Computing that field from psi as if it were weber per radian gives a ratio of 1 when the assumption holds and 2*pi when psi is really in weber, so the two answers are a factor 2*pi apart and the test is decisive rather than a threshold on a continuum. ParameterTypeUnitDescription equilibriumEquilibriumData-Must carry ip, a closed lcfs, and a psi map on its r and z grid; anything missing yields (None, None). ReturnsTypeUnitDescription tuple of (int or None, float or None)-(e_Bp, ratio). e_Bp is 0 for a weber-per-radian psi (COCOS 1-8) and 1 for a weber psi (COCOS 11-18), or None when the inputs are unavailable or the ratio lands near neither answer. ratio is the measured loop integral over mu0*|Ip|. Processing steps. Close the LCFS contour and compute the poloidal field on it with vaft.process.equilibrium.poloidal_field_at_boundary in the weber-per-radian form; only the magnitude matters. Integrate it along the contour by the trapezoidal rule. Divide by mu0*|Ip|. Accept 0 or 1 if the ratio is within FLUX_EXPONENT_TOLERANCE of 1 or 2*pi; otherwise abstain. Defaults. FLUX_EXPONENT_TOLERANCE is 0.15, a numerical convenience rather than a physical threshold: a correct equilibrium lands within about half a percent, the residual being LCFS discretization, so the band is roughly thirty times the observed error while leaving the two acceptance windows far apart, at 0.85 to 1.15 against 5.34 to 7.23. Convention. Decides which storage family psi is in; it does not rescale psi and does not say which of the eight sign orientations applies. e_Bp is Sauter’s flux exponent: 0 means the 2*pi is not carried in psi, 1 means it is. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Abstains rather than picking the nearer of two wrong answers. A ratio near neither value is evidence the input is broken, a truncated LCFS or an ip that disagrees with the psi map, not evidence of a convention. Needs a 2-D psi map and an LCFS, so a profiles-only equilibrium cannot be classified. Provenance. Sauter and Medvedev (2013) for e_Bp and the storage families. Replaces the a argument of omas.identify_cocos, which is not usable here: it evaluates pi*B0*(a[i]-a[0])**2/(psi[i]-psi[0]) at the node adjacent to the axis, where the minor radius goes as sqrt(psi), so a linear reconstruction underestimates it and the estimate depends on its square. On the packaged VEST sample that picks the wrong family on a margin of 0.22 against 1.67, where this loop integral separates 1.004 from 6.31. identify_flux_exponent_from_q identify_flux_exponent_from_q(equilibrium, *, levels=None) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Decide weber versus weber per radian by rebuilding q on closed contours. The second, independent answer to the question identify_flux_exponent asks. The safety factor of a closed surface is q = |F|/(2*pi) * contour_integral(dl / (R |grad psi|)) when psi is in weber per radian, and 2*pi times that when psi is in weber, so comparing both reconstructions against the q profile the file already carries separates the two families. It needs q and F; it needs neither ip nor a boundary outline, which is exactly what identify_flux_exponent cannot do without. On the three real equilibria this was measured on the two agree; where they differ is that this one still answers when the current record is zero or the boundary outline is missing. ParameterTypeUnitDescription equilibriumEquilibriumData-Must carry r, z, psi, psi_axis, psi_boundary, psi_1d, q and f; anything missing is an abstention, not an error. levelsarray_like, optional-Normalized flux levels to trace, defaulting to CONTOUR_Q_LEVELS ReturnsTypeUnitDescription ContourQNormalization-exponent 0 for weber per radian and 1 for weber, or None with a reason when the measurement does not support either. Processing steps. Trace each requested level with vaft.process.equilibrium.extract_flux_surface_contours and keep the longest closed contour that encloses the magnetic axis; a level whose contours are all open or all off-axis contributes nothing. On each kept contour evaluate |grad psi| = R * B_p with vaft.process.equilibrium.poloidal_field_at_boundary in its weber-per-radian form and integrate dl / (R |grad psi|) by the midpoint rule. Form the two candidate safety factors, |F|/(2*pi) times that integral and 2*pi times the first, and take each one’s |ln(q_model / q_stored)| against the stored |q| interpolated to the level. Take the median of each across the surfaces and accept the smaller one, but only when it is itself within CONTOUR_Q_LOG_TOLERANCE. Defaults. CONTOUR_Q_LEVELS and CONTOUR_Q_MIN_SURFACES are legacy compatibility values, carried over from geqdsk_cocos.flux_normalization_diagnostic so the two agree surface for surface. CONTOUR_Q_LOG_TOLERANCE is a numerical convenience: the Ampere rung’s 15% band made symmetric in the ratio, so a model q 1.16 times too large and one 1.16 times too small are equally far out. A plain relative error is not symmetric and accepted the second while rejecting the first. Convention. Decides Sauter’s flux exponent e_Bp – whether the 2*pi is carried inside psi – and nothing else. It does not rescale psi, does not identify a sign orientation, and does not distinguish the eight indices within a family. q and F are compared by magnitude, because codes routinely emit abs(q) and the sign question belongs to validate_cocos. Applicability. Machine-independent. Needs a 2-D psi map with closed interior surfaces, so a profiles-only equilibrium cannot be classified. Limitations. Abstains rather than picking the nearer of two wrong answers. A q profile that disagrees with its own psi map – a rescaled psi, a q taken from a different solve – makes both hypotheses wrong, and this reports that rather than a family. Marching squares resolves a contour only to the grid cell, so the log-ratio has a floor set by the grid: it was 1e-5 to 4e-4 on 129-by-129 and 513-by-513 reconstructions, against a losing log-ratio of ln(2*pi) = 1.8379. Provenance. hsyun_GPEC library/geqdsk_cocos.py::flux_normalization_diagnostic on branch codex/gpec-flare-cocos-handshake, which is the method and the levels. Its acceptance rule was relative only – the winner had to beat the loser threefold, with no bar on the winner’s own agreement – and that accepts a decisive-looking wrong answer: measured on a real g-file with psi scaled by one half, the winning hypothesis is off by a factor of 2.00 and the separation is still 3.65, so the legacy returns “weber per radian, decisive” for a hypothesis its own measurement misses by a factor of two. The bar in step 4 is what rejects it (D-04), and it makes the threefold rule unreachable: the two hypotheses sit exactly ln(2*pi) apart, so a winner inside the band leaves a ratio of at least twelve. The separation is reported, not applied. Sauter and Medvedev (2013) for e_Bp and the storage families. validate_cocos validate_cocos(equilibrium, cocos=None, *, sigma_ip=None, sigma_b0=None) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Check an equilibrium against the Sauter Eq. 23 relations for one COCOS index. The check that catches a mislabelled file before its signs propagate into derived quantities. Never raises on an inconsistency: it returns a report and lets the caller decide whether a mismatch is fatal. ParameterTypeUnitDescription equilibriumEquilibriumData-The equilibrium to check. cocosint, optional-The convention to check against, 1 to 18. Defaults to the index recorded on the equilibrium’s own convention. sigma_ipint, optional-Sign of the plasma current, +1 or -1. Defaults to the sign of the equilibrium’s ip. sigma_b0int, optional-Sign of the vacuum toroidal field. Defaults to the sign of bt0. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription ValidationReport-One issue per violated relation, plus at most one cocos_unverifiable warning covering every relation whose inputs were missing. An empty report means every checkable relation held. Processing steps. Resolve the target index and the two reference signs from the arguments, falling back to the equilibrium’s own convention and field signs. Measure the observed signs with cocos_consistency_signs. Compare each against the sign Eq. 23 requires for that index, collecting the mismatches. Collapse every unverifiable relation into a single warning rather than one issue each. Convention. Checks consistency with a convention; it does not identify one and does not convert. A mismatch on q is reported at warning severity rather than error, because codes commonly emit abs(q) and a sign disagreement there is not on its own evidence of a wrong index. Every other relation is an error. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Only four of Eq. 23’s six relations are checkable against vaft.data.equilibrium.EquilibriumData as it stands; j_phi and phi_tor have no field to read and are always unverifiable. A passing report therefore means “consistent as far as the stored fields can say”, not “the index is correct”. Provenance. Sauter and Medvedev (2013), Eq. 23 for the relations and Sect. IV for the rule that a q sign mismatch is a warning, not a rejection. Refreshing this snapshot From a checkout of the develop branch, run: python -m vaft.process.catalog --output docs/_data/process_catalog.yml The snapshot records the SHA-256 of every vaft/process/*.py source file; documentation validation compares them when VAFT_REGISTRY_SOURCE points to the corresponding source checkout. The same text is available offline as vaft.process.describe("<name>"), vaft.process.search("<text>") and vaft.process.list_processes(category="<category>").

/vaft/develop/reference/process/profile/.title: Process reference: profile
/vaft/develop/reference/process/profile/.body: This page is generated from the docstrings of vaft/process/profile.py: 15 public functions. The category overview and notation come from the module docstring; every entry below is what vaft.process.describe("profile.<name>") prints. Back to the process reference index. Overview The chain, and where each step’s state changes:: measured diagnostic points (R, Z, value) -> equilibrium-mapped coordinates: psi_norm, rho_pol_norm = sqrt(psi_norm), rho_tor_norm from the equilibrium's own Phi(psi) [MappedPositions] -> coordinate-selected profile points (default rho_tor_norm) -> fitted callable in that coordinate [FittedProfile] -> equilibrium-grid profile, stored on grid.rho_tor_norm / psi / rho_pol_norm with the fit's provenance beside it [core_profiles] Everything here is machine-independent. The radial coordinate to fit in, the statistical Ti/Te ratio for a Thomson-only slice, and their provenance are arguments; on VEST the pipeline (vaft.code.efit.build_kinetic_core_profiles) resolves them from vest.yaml through vaft.machine_mapping.core_profiles.vest_core_profiles_policy. This module holds no VEST number (issue #420). SymbolMeaningUnit psi_normnormalized poloidal flux, (psi - psi_axis)/(psi_boundary - psi_axis)- rho_pol_normsqrt(psi_norm)- rho_tor_normnormalized toroidal-flux radius, sqrt(Phi/Phi_boundary), Phi = int q dpsi [-] T_e, T_ielectron, ion temperatureeV n_eelectron densitym^-3 V_tortoroidal ion velocitym/s pthermal pressure, e n_e (T_e + T_i)Pa Three radial coordinates, never interchangeable: rho_tor_norm is not sqrt(psi_norm) except for a flat-q cylinder. A fit is a function of exactly one of them and carries which; core_profiles evaluates it on the equilibrium grid expressed in that coordinate. Parameter names that still say rho (rho_points, the deprecated mapped_rho_position) predate the choice and mean “the fit coordinate”. Quasi-neutral single main ion H+ with n_i = n_e; all electrons thermal. Functions compare_flux_mapping — Map one diagnostic’s channels through several equilibria, to see how much the mapping moves them. core_profiles — Evaluate fitted kinetic profiles on the equilibrium grid and store them as a profiles_1d slice. core_profiles_from_eq — Build a synthetic core_profiles slice from the equilibrium pressure and an axis T_e. core_profiles_from_eq_ratio — Build a synthetic core_profiles slice from the equilibrium pressure and a fixed n_e/T_e. equilibrium_mapping_charge_exchange — Map charge-exchange channel positions into the equilibrium’s radial coordinates. equilibrium_mapping_points — Map arbitrary (R, Z) points into the equilibrium’s radial coordinates. equilibrium_mapping_thomson_scattering — Map Thomson scattering channel positions into the equilibrium’s radial coordinates. export_electron_profile_txt — Write fitted electron profiles, sampled on a uniform grid, to a text file. fit_ti_te_ratio — Fit the proportionality coefficient alpha of Ti = alpha * Te. pedestal_top — Pedestal-top position of a profile, from an EPED-style fit. profile_fit_report_charge_exchange — Fit charge-exchange T_i and V_tor and report how well each fit reproduces its channels. profile_fit_report_thomson_scattering — Fit Thomson T_e and n_e and report how well each fit reproduces its channels. profile_fitting_charge_exchange — Fit charge-exchange T_i and V_tor profiles in a chosen radial coordinate. profile_fitting_thomson_scattering — Fit Thomson-scattering T_e and n_e profiles in a chosen radial coordinate. strip_electron_only_pressure — Drop slice-total pressure from every core_profiles slice with no ion temperature. compare_flux_mapping compare_flux_mapping(ods, equilibria, *, diagnostic='thomson_scattering', time=None) Machine-independent. Map one diagnostic’s channels through several equilibria, to see how much the mapping moves them. A profile’s radial coordinate is borrowed from an equilibrium, so two reconstructions of the same instant – a magnetics-only EFIT and a kinetic one, say – place the same channel at different psi_norm and rho_tor_norm. This maps the channels through each and returns the records side by side, keyed as the equilibria were. ParameterTypeUnitDescription odsODS-Carries the diagnostic’s channel positions. equilibriamapping of str to GEQDSK, ODS or mapping-The equilibria to compare, each anything equilibrium_mapping_thomson_scattering accepts; a path to a GEQDSK file is read with vaft.data.eqdsk.read_geqdsk when that reader is available. diagnosticstr, optional-"thomson_scattering" or "charge_exchange". timefloat, optionalsMap each ODS equilibrium through its slice nearest this time (as the mappers’ time); None keeps each one’s first slice. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription dict of str to MappedPositions-One record per equilibrium, in the order given, NaN outside that equilibrium’s LCFS. Raises. ValueError An unknown diagnostic. Assumptions. The channels’ (R, Z) are the same for every equilibrium; only the flux map changes. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Each ODS equilibrium contributes its first time slice unless time is given; pass the diagnostic’s time to pair the slices by time. Provenance. The mappers equilibrium_mapping_thomson_scattering and equilibrium_mapping_charge_exchange, applied once per equilibrium. core_profiles core_profiles(ods, time_ms, mapped_positions=None, n_e_function=None, T_e_function=None, tol_ms=0.1, T_i_function=None, V_tor_function=None, ti_mapped_positions=None, rho_points=100, time_tolerance_ms=1.0, geq=None, ti_te_fallback=True, ti_te_ratio=None, *, coordinate=None, ti_te_ratio_record=None, mapped_rho_position=None, ti_mapped_rho_position=None) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Evaluate fitted kinetic profiles on the equilibrium grid and store them as a profiles_1d slice. The fits are functions of one radial coordinate – the one they were made in, carried by FittedProfile or named by coordinate for a plain callable – and are evaluated on the equilibrium’s grid expressed in that same coordinate, so a fit in rho_tor_norm is never evaluated at a psi_norm value. What was fitted, in which coordinate, and where any assumed number came from is written beside the profile. ParameterTypeUnitDescription odsODS-Mutated in place: gains or replaces the core_profiles.profiles_1d slice at time_ms. time_msfloatmsTime of the slice. mapped_positionsMappedPositions or np.ndarray, optional-Thomson channel positions from equilibrium_mapping_thomson_scattering; required with an electron fit. A bare array is the deprecated pre-#420 form and is accepted only with coordinate="psi_norm". n_e_functionFittedProfile or callable, optionalm^-3Electron density fit. T_e_functionFittedProfile or callable, optionaleVElectron temperature fit. tol_msfloat, optionalmsAn existing slice within this of time_ms is replaced. T_i_functionFittedProfile or callable, optionaleVIon temperature fit from the charge-exchange fitter; when given, the ion block carries the real T_i and pressure_thermal is written. V_tor_functionFittedProfile or callable, optionalm/sToroidal ion velocity fit. ti_mapped_positionsMappedPositions or np.ndarray, optional-Charge-exchange channel positions, for the ion fit metadata. rho_pointsint, optional-Size of the uniform fallback grid when no equilibrium slice matches. time_tolerance_msfloat, optionalmsTolerance for matching the Thomson and equilibrium times. geqGEQDSK, optional-The equilibrium the mapping used; its 1-D grid is preferred over the ODS equilibrium so the profile lands on the same surfaces. ti_te_fallbackbool, optional-With no ion fit, still write an ion temperature from T_e. ti_te_ratiofloat, optional-Coefficient for that fallback: T_i = ratio * T_e and pressure_thermal = e n_e (1 + ratio) T_e; None keeps the legacy T_i = T_e and writes no pressure. Resolved by the pipeline from the machine policy; this function holds no value. coordinatestr, optional-Required when the fits are plain callables; must agree with every FittedProfile given. ti_te_ratio_recordstr, optional-Provenance text for the ratio (value, status, source), stored beside the ion temperature; the pipeline passes the policy’s own record. mapped_rho_positionMappedPositions or np.ndarray, optional-Deprecated name for mapped_positions. ti_mapped_rho_positionMappedPositions or np.ndarray, optional-Deprecated name for ti_mapped_positions. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription ODS-The same object, updated. Raises. ValueError No electron and no ion fit; an electron fit without positions; fits in different coordinates; a ratio that is not finite and non-negative; no Thomson time within tolerance. TypeError A plain callable without coordinate, or a bare position array without coordinate="psi_norm". CoordinateUnavailableError The mapping cannot supply the fit’s coordinate. Processing steps. Establish the fit coordinate from the fit objects (or coordinate) and check they agree. Read the measured Thomson values at the nearest time. Take the equilibrium 1-D grid – from geq, else the ODS slice at this time – as (rho_tor_norm, psi, psi_norm); express it in the fit coordinate; without one, use a uniform grid in that coordinate. Evaluate every fit on that grid; apply the ion fallback if needed. Replace any slice at the same time, write grid, electrons, ions, pressure, per-channel fit metadata and provenance. Input semantics. Fitted: callables of one radial coordinate, from profile_fitting_thomson_scattering / profile_fitting_charge_exchange, plus the measured channel values and their equilibrium-mapped positions. Output semantics. Stored, on the equilibrium grid: grid.rho_tor_norm, grid.psi and grid.rho_pol_norm when an equilibrium slice exists, else only the coordinate the fit is actually in. *_fit.measured are measured, *_fit.reconstructed are the fit at the measured points; a ratio-derived ion temperature is inferred and says so. Defaults. ti_te_ratio = None is a legacy compatibility value: the pre-#420 behaviour writes T_i = T_e and no pressure. The VEST value is resolved by vaft.machine_mapping.core_profiles.vest_core_profiles_policy and passed in by vaft.code.efit.build_kinetic_core_profiles. tol_ms = 0.1 and time_tolerance_ms = 1.0 are numerical conveniences. Convention. The fit coordinate is one of rho_tor_norm, rho_pol_norm, psi_norm; the equilibrium grid supplies all three (rho_pol_norm = sqrt(psi_norm); rho_tor_norm from the equilibrium, never from psi_norm). Quasi-neutral single main ion H+, n_i = n_e. pressure_thermal = e n_e (T_e + T_i) [Pa] with temperatures in eV. Assumptions. All electrons are thermal (an ohmic plasma); one hydrogenic main ion with no impurity dilution; the equilibrium at time_ms is the one the channels were mapped through. Applicability. Machine-independent. Every machine-specific number – the coordinate convention, the Ti/Te ratio, its provenance – arrives as an argument; for VEST the pipeline resolves them from vest.yaml. Limitations. Only the first equilibrium time slice of geq is used. The charge-exchange *_fit metadata is best-effort and its failure is reported, not raised. A slice produced before #420 has no *_fit.parameters; that absence is the signature of a legacy product fitted in psi_norm. Provenance. Per-slice fit records in electrons.{density,temperature}_fit.parameters and ion.0.temperature_fit.parameters, and one line per slice in core_profiles.code.parameters; issue #420. core_profiles_from_eq core_profiles_from_eq(ods, Te0_eV, rho_fit=None, tol_ms=0.1, eq_time_index=0) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Build a synthetic core_profiles slice from the equilibrium pressure and an axis T_e. ParameterTypeUnitDescription odsODS-Carries the equilibrium slice; gains the core_profiles slice. Te0_eVfloateVElectron temperature on axis. rho_fitarray_like, optional-rho_tor_norm grid to write on; None for 100 uniform points. tol_msfloat, optionalmsAn existing slice within this of the equilibrium time is replaced. eq_time_indexint, optional-Which equilibrium time slice. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription ODS-The same object, updated. Raises. ValueError Non-1-D or non-finite equilibrium profiles, or non-positive axis pressure. Processing steps. Interpolate the equilibrium pressure(rho_tor_norm) onto rho_fit. g = sqrt(p / p(0)); T_e = Te0 g; n_e = p(0) / (2 e Te0) g. Write electrons and a quasi-neutral H+ ion with T_i = T_e. Input semantics. Reconstructed: the equilibrium pressure profile. Output semantics. Synthetic: profiles consistent with that pressure under an assumed shape, not measured. ParameterTypeUnitDescription odsomas.ODSn/aMutated in place. An ODS with no core_profiles is left alone. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription Nonen/aThe ODS is edited in place. Assumptions. Presence of ion.0.temperature marks a slice whose ion temperature was measured rather than assumed. The builders uphold that by refusing to write an ion block from a Ti/Te fallback. Applicability. Machine-independent. The rule follows from what the IMAS leaves mean, not from any VEST diagnostic. The same text is available offline as vaft.process.describe("<name>"), vaft.process.search("<text>") and vaft.process.list_processes(category="<category>").

/vaft/develop/reference/process/atomic/.title: Process reference: atomic
/vaft/develop/reference/process/atomic/.body: This page is generated from the docstrings of vaft/process/atomic.py: 5 public functions. The category overview and notation come from the module docstring; every entry below is what vaft.process.describe("atomic.<name>") prints. Back to the process reference index. Overview This module owns profile selection, time alignment, impurity-density fallback and volume integration. Numerical atomic physics remains in vaft.formula.atomic and ADF11 file access in vaft.data.open_adas. Which impurity species to include and what fraction to assume for them is machine policy, resolved by the pipeline (vaft.omas.formula_wrapper.compute_power_balance from vest.yaml on VEST) and passed in; this module holds no such number (issue #420). SymbolMeaningUnit n_eelectron densitym^-3 n_impimpurity densitym^-3 T_eelectron temperatureeV L_Zline-radiation cooling coefficient of species ZW m^3 epsilonline emissivity, n_e n_imp L_ZW/m^3 P_lineradiated line power, int epsilon dVW Vcumulative enclosed plasma volumem^3 rho_tor_normnormalized toroidal-flux radius- Functions compute_line_radiation_power_series — Line-radiation power for matched equilibrium slices, from the stored kinetic profiles. compute_time_match_atol — An absolute time-matching tolerance adapted to the native time spacing. find_time_match_index — Index of the time closest to target_time, within the adaptive tolerance. integrate_emissivity_profile — Integrate an emissivity profile to a total radiated power. normalize_atomic_symbol — Normalize an element or ion label to a supported atomic symbol. compute_line_radiation_power_series compute_line_radiation_power_series(ods, eq_indices, eq_times, volume_series, line_radiation_species=None, impurity_fractions=None, Z_eff=None, *, return_assumptions=False) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Line-radiation power for matched equilibrium slices, from the stored kinetic profiles. For each species and time slice the local emissivity is epsilon = n_e n_imp L_Z(n_e, T_e) and the power P = int epsilon dV. ParameterTypeUnitDescription odsODS-Carries core_profiles.profiles_1d and equilibrium.time_slice. eq_indiceslist of int-Equilibrium slice indices to evaluate. eq_timesarray_likesTime of each of those slices. volume_seriesarray_likem^3Total plasma volume of each slice, for the integration fallback. line_radiation_specieslist of str, optional-Species to include; None for every species that has a configured fraction or an ion density profile in the ODS. impurity_fractionsdict of str to float, optional-n_imp / n_e per species, used when the ODS carries no profile for it; None means no assumption. Z_efffloat, optional-Effective charge, used only to infer a single species’ fraction when nothing else is known. return_assumptionsbool, optional-Also return what each species’ density was taken from. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription np.ndarray or tuple of (np.ndarray, dict)WNon-negative line-radiation power per eq_indices entry, and with return_assumptions a dict of species, per-species impurity_source (profile, configured, inferred_from_zeff or none), the impurity_fraction used, and z_eff. Raises. ValueError Mismatched eq_times / volume_series lengths, non-finite times, an unrecognized species label, or a negative or non-finite fraction. Processing steps. Match each equilibrium time to a core_profiles slice (find_time_match_index); an unmatched slice radiates nothing. Interpolate n_e, T_e from the slice’s rho_tor_norm onto the equilibrium’s rho_tor_norm (constant edge extrapolation). For each species, take n_imp / n_e from, in order: the slice’s own ion density profile; impurity_fractions; a single-species inference from Z_eff; else zero with one warning per species. L_Z from the ADAS tables [FORMULA]; epsilon = L_Z n_e n_imp. integrate_emissivity_profile per species, summed; clipped at zero. Input semantics. Stored kinetic profiles (fitted or synthetic) on their core_profiles grid, plus the equilibrium grid and volume. Output semantics. Synthetic: a modelled diagnostic-like quantity, not a measurement. Defaults. impurity_fractions = None and line_radiation_species = None mean no assumption. The VEST carbon and oxygen fractions that used to be this function’s defaults are machine-specific settings, each an assumed value in vest.yaml resolved by the pipeline. Z_eff = None disables the single-species inference, a numerical convenience. Convention. The radial coordinate is rho_tor_norm throughout: the core_profiles grid and the equilibrium profiles_1d both carry it and are interpolated against each other in it. n_i for the impurity is fraction * n_e where a fraction is used; Z_eff inference assumes hydrogenic main ions, n_imp/n_e = (Z_eff - 1)/(Z(Z - 1)). Assumptions. Coronal equilibrium for L_Z; one impurity species at a time with no mutual dilution; the core_profiles slice at the matched time describes the equilibrium slice. Applicability. Machine-independent. Species and fractions arrive as arguments. Limitations. Every failure mode – no core_profiles, no matching time, no n_e or T_e, ADAS data unavailable, no fraction known – yields zero for that slice or species with a logged warning rather than an error, to keep an offline power balance running; the returned assumptions are how a caller can tell. A core_profiles slice stored on rho_pol_norm only (no equilibrium at its time) has no rho_tor_norm and is skipped. Provenance. ADAS tables [ADAS] through the cooling-coefficient kernel [FORMULA]. compute_time_match_atol compute_time_match_atol(time_array, base_atol=1e-06) Machine-independent. An absolute time-matching tolerance adapted to the native time spacing. max(base_atol, 0.25 * min(diff(unique_finite_times))), which absorbs floating-point drift in a time coordinate without ever matching an adjacent physical slice. ParameterTypeUnitDescription time_arraynp.ndarraysThe time coordinate to be matched against. base_atolfloat, optionalsFloor on the tolerance. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription floatsThe tolerance; base_atol when fewer than two distinct finite times exist. Raises. ValueError base_atol non-finite or negative. Defaults. base_atol = 1e-6 s and the factor 0.25 are numerical conveniences: a quarter of the smallest spacing can never reach the neighbouring slice. Applicability. Machine-independent. find_time_match_index find_time_match_index(time_array, target_time) Machine-independent. Index of the time closest to target_time, within the adaptive tolerance. ParameterTypeUnitDescription time_arraynp.ndarraysThe time coordinate. target_timefloatsThe time to match. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription int or None-Index of the closest time within compute_time_match_atol; None for an empty array, a non-finite target, or no candidate within tolerance. Applicability. Machine-independent. integrate_emissivity_profile integrate_emissivity_profile(emissivity_profile, volume_profile, total_volume) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Integrate an emissivity profile to a total radiated power. ParameterTypeUnitDescription emissivity_profilenp.ndarrayW/m^3Local emissivity on the radial grid. volume_profilenp.ndarray or Nonem^3Cumulative enclosed volume on the same grid, or None. total_volumefloatm^3Total plasma volume, for the fallback. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription floatWP = int epsilon dV, or the fallback, or 0. Processing steps. If volume_profile is given, matches the emissivity’s shape and has at least two finite points spanning a non-zero volume: trapezoidal integration of epsilon against V, in volume order. Else, if total_volume is finite and positive: nanmean(epsilon) * total_volume. Else 0. Convention. volume_profile is the cumulative enclosed volume V(rho), so dV is its difference; it is not a shell volume. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. The two fallbacks are silent: a volume profile of the wrong length drops to the mean-times-volume estimate, and a missing volume to zero, with no warning from this function. normalize_atomic_symbol normalize_atomic_symbol(label) Machine-independent. Normalize an element or ion label to a supported atomic symbol. Full English names and charge-decorated labels are accepted – carbon6+ gives C, neon gives Ne. ParameterTypeUnitDescription labelstr, bytes or None-The label as found in an ODS ion.label or a species list. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription str or None-The symbol, or None for an unrecognized label so the caller decides whether absence is fatal. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Only the elements in the module’s table are recognized (H through W, the common tokamak species); isotopes D and T map to their own symbols. Refreshing this snapshot From a checkout of the develop branch, run: python -m vaft.process.catalog --output docs/_data/process_catalog.yml The snapshot records the SHA-256 of every vaft/process/*.py source file; documentation validation compares them when VAFT_REGISTRY_SOURCE points to the corresponding source checkout. The same text is available offline as vaft.process.describe("<name>"), vaft.process.search("<text>") and vaft.process.list_processes(category="<category>").

/vaft/develop/reference/process/equilibr.title: Process reference: equilibrium
/vaft/develop/reference/process/equilibr.body: This page is generated from the docstrings of vaft/process/equilibrium.py: 59 public functions. The category overview and notation come from the module docstring; every entry below is what vaft.process.describe("equilibrium.<name>") prints. Back to the process reference index. Overview Physics only. Nothing here reads or writes an ODS: every function takes arrays and returns arrays or plain records, so the same code serves a GEQDSK, an ODS slice and an analytic model. The adapters that turn those into one record, and the parametric models fitted to them, live in _equilibrium_parametric and are re-exported through this module, which is their stable import location. What the module does, in the order a flux map is usually consumed:: psi(R, Z) on a grid -> radial coordinates: psi_norm, and the toroidal radius through q -> flux surfaces: contours, their shape, their averages -> fields: the poloidal field from psi, the toroidal field from F -> global scalars: diamagnetism, the Shafranov integrals, force balance SymbolMeaningUnit psipoloidal fluxWb/rad psi_norm(psi - psi_axis)/(psi_boundary - psi_axis)- Fpoloidal current function, R*B_phiT m B_ppoloidal field magnitudeT qsafety factor- kSauter Eq. 20 prefactor carrying sign and 2*pi- Flux is per radian unless a function says otherwise. The poloidal field from psi carries a factor k = sigma_RphiZ * sigma_Bp / (2*pi)**e_Bp [1], which folds the orientation sign and the 2pi normalization together. A function that forms a field from psi takes a COCOS index, and with none it uses the historical weber-per-radian form. Getting this wrong scales the field by 2pi and the poloidal beta by its square, plausibly and silently. A function that takes a precomputed field instead inherits whatever convention produced it and cannot check it. Three radial coordinates, never interchangeable. rho_tor_norm equals sqrt(psi_norm), which is rho_pol_norm, only for a flat safety factor. derive_radial_coordinates returns all three with an explicit record of which is unavailable and why. Flux maps are indexed (R, Z), matching the IMAS two-dimensional profile layout. Boundary contours run counter-clockwise, because the Shafranov outward normal is only outward then. Functions as_equilibrium — Adapt a GEQDSK, ODS, IMAS handle, or native model to one equilibrium record. calculate_average_boundary_poloidal_field — Contour-length average of the poloidal field around a closed boundary. calculate_diamagnetism — Diamagnetism from its volume-integral definition. calculate_q_profile_from_psi — Calculate the safety factor profile q(psi) from a 2D poloidal flux map and F(psi). calculate_reconstructed_diamagnetic_flux — Diamagnetic flux reconstructed from the equilibrium’s own toroidal field. check_equilibrium_requirements — Whether an equilibrium carries what a named algorithm needs to run. compare_contours — How far apart two closed contours are, point to curve. computed_diamagnetism_from_phi — EFIT-style diamagnetism from an already-computed diamagnetic flux. connection_length_map — Connection length of the field line through each of many starting points. contour_shape_parameters — Shape parameters of one closed flux-surface contour. convert_cocos — Convert an equilibrium between two explicitly known COCOS conventions. derive_boundary_representation — Classify the plasma boundary and derive its geometric diagnostics. derive_global_descriptors — Global scalar descriptors of one equilibrium, each with its derivation record. derive_radial_coordinates — The three normalized radial coordinates, each with its derivation record. efit_virial_volume_integrals — EFIT-style weighted volume integrals for the virial closures. ejiri_mirror_geometry — Ejiri mirror-confinement proxy for one magnetic snapshot. equilibrium_field_on_grid — (B_R, B_Z, B_phi) on the whole (R, Z) grid, each (nR, nZ). evaluate_miller — Points on a Miller-parameterized flux surface at given poloidal angles. evaluate_solovev — Evaluate an analytic Solov’ev equilibrium on a set of points. extract_flux_surface_contours — Iso-flux contours at requested normalized levels, by marching squares. find_rational_surfaces — Where a toroidal mode resonates: the surfaces with q = m / n. find_stationary_points — Locate the O-points and saddles of psi to sub-grid accuracy. fit_miller_sequence — Fit Miller parameters across a sequence of flux surfaces, with radial derivatives. fit_miller_surface — Fit the Miller shape parameters to one closed flux-surface contour. flux_surface_quantities — Flux-surface averages and shape parameters on each normalized flux level. fractional_cell_weights_from_boundary — Fractional area of each grid cell that lies inside the plasma boundary. grad_shafranov_operator — The Grad-Shafranov elliptic operator on a rectangular grid. grad_shafranov_residual — How far an equilibrium is from satisfying its own force balance, surface by surface. integrate_romero_closure — Integrate Romero’s first-order closure from a boundary-voltage history. lab_to_straight_field_line — Relabel a geometric poloidal angle into the straight-field-line one. make_equilibrium_field_interpolator — Build a callable giving the full magnetic field anywhere on one time slice. make_vacuum_field_interpolator — Build a callable giving the vacuum magnetic field anywhere on one grid. miller_surfaces — A family of Miller surfaces for a shape scan. parallel_current_from_toroidal — Convert a shell toroidal driven current to the IMAS parallel current. plasma_cell_weights — Fraction of each grid cell that is plasma, from the boundary outline when there is one. poloidal_field_at_boundary — Poloidal field on a boundary contour, from the flux map by bicubic spline. prepare_boundary_for_shafranov — Condition a boundary contour into the form the Shafranov integrals require. psi_to_radial — Inboard and outboard major radius of each flux value, along the axis row. psi_to_rho — Normalized toroidal-flux radius at one poloidal flux value, by integrating q. psi_to_rz — Map a flux-surface profile onto the two-dimensional grid through psi. r_at_z_extremum — Major radius where a contour reaches its highest or lowest point. radial_to_psi — Poloidal flux at a major radius on the midplane row of the flux map. resistive_layer_at — Resistivity and mass density at flux surfaces someone else located. resistive_layer_parameters — Resistivity and mass density at each rational surface of a toroidal mode. rho_to_psi — Poloidal flux at one normalized toroidal-flux radius, by root finding. romero_flux_balance — Romero’s exact voltage and volt-second balance over a sampled discharge. scale_boundary_conformal — Scale a closed boundary about a centre, giving a contour conformal to it. shafranov_integrals — The three Shafranov boundary integrals and the virial coefficient. solovev_example — Build a shaped analytic Solov’ev equilibrium in a chosen boundary topology. solovev_to_equilibrium — Export an analytic Solov’ev model as a gridded equilibrium record. solve_solovev_constraints — Solve for the Solov’ev coefficients that satisfy a set of geometric constraints. straight_field_line_angle_on_grid — The PEST straight-field-line angle on every node of a flux map. straight_field_line_map — The PEST straight-field-line poloidal angle of a flux map, built once. straight_field_line_tables — Per-surface tables taking the geometric poloidal angle to the code’s own. trace_field_line — Trace one magnetic field line through the equilibrium field. validate_equilibrium — Deprecated compatibility wrapper for check_equilibrium_requirements. virial_alpha_conformal_annulus — Virial closure coefficient from a thin annulus conformal to the LCFS. virial_alpha_thin_annulus — Virial closure coefficient in the thin-annulus limit, from the boundary field. volume_average — Volume average of a gridded quantity over the confined region. as_equilibrium as_equilibrium(source, *, time_index=0, profile_index=0, convention=None) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Adapt a GEQDSK, ODS, IMAS handle, or native model to one equilibrium record. The single entry point every algorithm here goes through, so that they operate on one normalized shape regardless of where the equilibrium came from. ParameterTypeUnitDescription sourceEquilibriumData, ODS, GEQDSK, IMAS equilibrium IDS, path or mapping-A record is returned as is, or converted when a convention is asserted; a path or path-like is read as a GEQDSK; an object exposing an OMAS export is exported first; a native IDS root is wrapped. time_indexint, optional-Which time slice to take from a multi-slice source. profile_indexint, optional-Which 2-D profile grid to take from a slice carrying more than one. conventionint, optional-A COCOS index the caller asserts for source, 1 to 18. When given it always wins over identification, and the result is converted to it. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription EquilibriumData-The normalized record, with its convention set from the assertion when one was made and from identification otherwise. Convention. Normalizes shape, not convention: the returned record is not converted to any internal standard unless convention asks for it, so its psi may be in weber or weber per radian and only convention.psi_per_radian says which. A record built without a convention reports neither, and downstream field calculations then fall back to the historical per-radian form. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. A GEQDSK is identified as a two-dimensional grid by the presence of its characteristic keys, so a mapping that happens to carry them is treated as one. Only the requested time slice and profile grid are read; everything else in a multi-slice source is discarded. Provenance. The per-source adapters below preserve each format’s own layout conventions; see vaft.process.cocos.identify_convention for how the convention is inferred when the caller does not assert one. calculate_average_boundary_poloidal_field calculate_average_boundary_poloidal_field(R_bdry, Z_bdry, B_p_bdry) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Contour-length average of the poloidal field around a closed boundary. ParameterTypeUnitDescription R_bdryarray_likemMajor radius of the contour points. Z_bdryarray_likemHeight of the contour points. B_p_bdryarray_likeTPoloidal field magnitude at those points. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription floatTThe average poloidal field, the contour integral of the field over the contour length. Convention. Weighted by arc length, not by point count, so an unevenly sampled contour still gives the physical average. The midpoint rule is used between consecutive points, and the contour is treated as closed. This is the normalizing field that the poloidal beta and the diamagnetism are taken against, so it must come from the same convention as the field that produced it. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Midpoint rule on the given points, so a coarsely sampled contour underweights regions of high curvature. Takes the field magnitudes as given and cannot check they were computed in a consistent convention. Provenance. The definition used with shafranov_integrals and calculate_diamagnetism as their reference field. calculate_diamagnetism calculate_diamagnetism(R_grid, Z_grid, psi_RZ, psi_axis, psi_lcfs, psiN_1d, f_1d, f_vac_val, B_pa, V_p=None, weights=None) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Diamagnetism from its volume-integral definition. ParameterTypeUnitDescription R_gridarray_likemMajor-radius grid axis. Z_gridarray_likemHeight grid axis. psi_RZarray_likeWb/radPoloidal flux on the grid, indexed (R, Z). psi_axisfloatWb/radPoloidal flux on the magnetic axis. psi_lcfsfloatWb/radPoloidal flux at the last closed flux surface. psiN_1darray_like-Normalized poloidal flux the poloidal-current profile is given on. f_1darray_likeT mPoloidal current function F = R*B_phi on that abscissa. f_vac_valfloatT mThe same function at the boundary, standing in for the vacuum field B_pafloatTBoundary-average poloidal field, the normalizing scale, strictly positive V_pfloat, optionalm^3Plasma volume. Computed from the same grid and mask when not given weightsarray_like, optional-Fraction of each cell inside the plasma, from plasma_cell_weights; replaces the normalized-flux mask when given. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription float-The diamagnetism, positive for a diamagnetic plasma and negative for a paramagnetic one. Raises. ValueError The boundary-average poloidal field is not positive. Convention. mu_i = (1/(B_pa^2 * V)) * integral (B_tv^2 - B_t^2) dV, with the toroidal fields taken as the poloidal current function over the major radius and the axisymmetric volume element. Positive means the plasma reduced the toroidal field. A result of the unexpected sign usually means the vacuum proxy was taken on axis rather than at the boundary, or that the poloidal current profile’s sign convention disagrees with the equilibrium it came from. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. The same per-cell boundary mask as volume_average, so the boundary is resolved only to the grid. The vacuum field is a single boundary value rather than a profile. Provenance. The volume-integral definition of diamagnetism; the surface-integral form is calculate_reconstructed_diamagnetic_flux, and the two should agree for a consistent equilibrium. calculate_q_profile_from_psi calculate_q_profile_from_psi(psi_grid, R, Z, f_profile, psi_axis=None, psi_boundary=None, levels_norm=None, *, axis_rz=None, boundary=None, cocos=11, sigma_ip=1, sigma_b0=1, min_points=16, return_details=False) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Calculate the safety factor profile q(psi) from a 2D poloidal flux map and F(psi). ParameterTypeUnitDescription psi_gridarray_likeWb or Wb/radPoloidal flux on the grid, shaped (len(R), len(Z)), in the convention cocos specifies. Rarray_likemMajor-radius grid axis. Zarray_likemHeight grid axis. f_profilefloat, array_like, callable, or tuple of array_likeT mPoloidal current function F = R B_phi, as a scalar float, 1D array, callable f(psi), or tuple (psi_f, f_values). psi_axisfloat, optionalWb or Wb/radPoloidal flux at the magnetic axis, in the convention cocos specifies. psi_boundaryfloat, optionalWb or Wb/radPoloidal flux at the plasma boundary/LCFS, in the convention cocos specifies. levels_normsequence of float, optional-Normalized flux levels to evaluate on, 0 on axis and 1 at the boundary. axis_rztuple of float, optionalmMagnetic axis coordinates (R_axis, Z_axis). boundarytuple of np.ndarray, optionalmBoundary outline (R_bdry, Z_bdry). cocosint, optional-COCOS coordinate convention index (1-8, 11-18) describing the input conventions and target sign for q. sigma_ipint, optional-Sign of plasma current (+1 or -1) in the equilibrium coordinate system. sigma_b0int, optional-Sign of toroidal field (+1 or -1) in the equilibrium coordinate system. min_pointsint, optional-Fewest contour vertices a level needs before it is treated as resolved. return_detailsbool, optional-Whether to return diagnostic parameters and the full flux-surface quantities alongside the safety factor array. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription np.ndarray or dict of str to Any-If return_details is False, returns a 1D array of safety factor values q on levels_norm [-]. If return_details is True, returns a dict with keys "q", "levels_norm", "psi_levels", "q_axis", "q_95", and "surfaces". Raises. ValueError The flux map is not shaped to (len(R), len(Z)), psi_axis or psi_boundary cannot be determined or are equal, or f_profile format is invalid. Processing steps. Validate grid dimensions and identify the flux conversion factor from cocos. Normalize or deduce psi_axis and psi_boundary, converting to Wb/rad if necessary. Evaluate and interpolate f_profile onto the requested levels_norm. Call flux_surface_quantities to trace contours and compute geometric averages. Apply on-axis quadratic extrapolation in radius (linear in normalized flux $\psi_N$) to resolve $q_0$. Attach the COCOS sign factor $\sigma_q$ and package the output. Defaults. levels_norm defaults to 65 points from 0 to 1 (numerical convenience). cocos=11 matches the IMAS standard data dictionary convention. Convention. In Sauter and Medvedev (2013), the safety factor is defined as: \(q(\psi) = \frac{F(\psi)}{2\pi} \oint \frac{dl_p}{R^2 B_p} = \frac{F(\psi)}{2\pi} (2\pi)^{e_{B_p}} \oint \frac{dl_p}{R |\nabla\psi|}\) Expressed in terms of the geometric flux-surface averages computed by flux_surface_quantities (which operates in Wb/rad, $e_{B_p} = 0$, $dV/d\psi$ per radian): \(q(\psi) = \sigma \cdot \frac{F(\psi)}{(2\pi)^2} \left\langle \frac{1}{R^2} \right\rangle \frac{dV}{d\psi}\) where $\langle 1/R^2 \rangle$ is gm1, $dV/d\psi$ is dvolume_dpsi, and $\sigma$ is the orientation sign from Sauter Eq. 23: $\sigma_q = \sigma_{Ip} \sigma_{B0} \sigma_{\rho\theta\varphi}$. When cocos indicates full Weber storage ($e_{B_p} = 1$, COCOS 11-18), the input fluxes are divided by $2\pi$ to enter the contour tracing engine, and the resulting profile carries the exact COCOS-mandated sign. Applicability. Machine-independent. Works for any 2D tokamak poloidal flux map. Provenance. O. Sauter and S. Yu. Medvedev, Comput. Phys. Commun. 184 (2013) 293, Eq. (17) and Table I for COCOS relations and safety factor definitions. J. Wesson, Tokamaks, 4th ed., Oxford University Press (2011), Sec. 3.4. calculate_reconstructed_diamagnetic_flux calculate_reconstructed_diamagnetic_flux(R_grid, Z_grid, psi_RZ, psi_axis, psi_lcfs, psiN_1d, f_1d, f_vac_val, weights=None) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Diamagnetic flux reconstructed from the equilibrium’s own toroidal field. The surface integral of the difference between the plasma toroidal field and the vacuum field it displaces. Physics only: it reads no ODS and writes none. ParameterTypeUnitDescription R_gridarray_likemMajor-radius grid axis. Z_gridarray_likemHeight grid axis. psi_RZarray_likeWb/radPoloidal flux on the grid, indexed (R, Z). psi_axisfloatWb/radPoloidal flux on the magnetic axis. psi_lcfsfloatWb/radPoloidal flux at the last closed flux surface. psiN_1darray_like-Normalized poloidal flux the poloidal-current profile is given on. f_1darray_likeT mPoloidal current function F = R*B_phi on that abscissa. f_vac_valfloatT mThe same function at the boundary, standing in for the vacuum field weightsarray_like, optional-Fraction of each cell inside the plasma, from plasma_cell_weights; replaces the normalized-flux mask when given. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription floatWbThe reconstructed diamagnetic flux, negative for a diamagnetic plasma Processing steps. Map the poloidal current profile onto the grid through psi_to_rz. Form the plasma and vacuum toroidal fields as that function over the major radius. Integrate their difference over the cross-section inside the boundary. Convention. The sign follows the physics, not a storage choice: a diamagnetic plasma reduces the toroidal field inside it, so the integral is negative. Only the normalized flux enters, so the absolute unit of the three flux arguments cancels as long as they agree. The vacuum proxy must be taken at the boundary, not on axis, or the difference is offset everywhere. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. A cross-sectional integral on the grid, so the boundary is resolved only to the cell. The vacuum field is taken as a single boundary value rather than a profile, which is exact only where the poloidal current is flat outside the plasma. Provenance. The definition of diamagnetic flux as the toroidal-field deficit integrated over the plasma cross-section, in the form the EFIT-style workflow this package reproduces uses. check_equilibrium_requirements check_equilibrium_requirements(equilibrium, *, required_for='general') Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Whether an equilibrium carries what a named algorithm needs to run. A precondition, not a scientific verdict (issue #337): it answers “can the global, Miller, edge or Solov’ev algorithms be applied to this input”, which is why the answer depends on which one is asked about. Whether the equilibrium is credible is a different question, asked by vaft.validation (#72). Renamed from validate_equilibrium, which read as the latter and is now the name of the latter. ParameterTypeUnitDescription equilibriumEquilibriumData-The record to check. required_forstr, optional-Which requirement set to apply: general, global, miller, edge or solovev. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription ValidationReport-One issue per unmet requirement, at error severity for a missing or malformed field and warning severity for an ambiguous or self-contradictory convention. An empty report means the algorithm can run. Convention. Reports two convention problems without resolving either: an ambiguous COCOS, where identification left more than one candidate, and a declared COCOS that contradicts the signs actually observed.
