ReturnsTypeUnitDescription dict of str to Any-phi in radians, R and Z in metres, arc_length_m in metres, and termination_reason as a string. Processing steps. Integrate dR/dphi = R*B_R/B_phi and dZ/dphi = R*B_Z/B_phi by fixed-step fourth-order Runge-Kutta in the toroidal angle. After each step, test the termination conditions in order: leaving the limiting polygon, exceeding the path length, leaving the coordinate bounds, or a numerically zero toroidal field. For "both", trace each branch and concatenate them anchored at the start. Defaults. The one-degree step and the fifty-metre limit are numerical conveniences: fine enough to resolve a tokamak field line’s pitch, and long enough to reach a wall from anywhere inside a small machine. Convention. The toroidal angle is the integration variable, not path length or time, which is why a vanishing toroidal field terminates the trace rather than slowing it. Points are always returned in order of increasing angle whatever the direction traced. The arc length is cumulative along the returned array from zero at its first point, so for "both" it measures from the backward end and not from the start point. Applicability. Machine-independent. The wall polygon is where a machine’s own geometry enters, and it is supplied by the caller. Limitations. Fixed step, so accuracy is set by the step alone and there is no error control; a line near a separatrix, where the pitch changes fastest, is the least accurate. Terminating on the coordinate bounds is a safety net against extrapolating far outside the equilibrium grid, not a physical condition. Provenance. The field-line equations in toroidal-angle form; the field itself comes from make_equilibrium_field_interpolator. validate_equilibrium validate_equilibrium(equilibrium, *, required_for='general') Deprecated. Deprecated compatibility wrapper for check_equilibrium_requirements. virial_alpha_conformal_annulus virial_alpha_conformal_annulus(R_grid, Z_grid, B_R_grid, B_Z_grid, R_bdry, Z_bdry, thickness=0.1, samples_per_axis=5) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Virial closure coefficient from a thin annulus conformal to the LCFS. alpha_2 = 2 * sum(R Bz^2 w dA) / sum(R Bp^2 w dA) over an annulus bounded by the boundary and a copy of it scaled by 1 - thickness. Obtains the closure coefficient without the volume integral over the plasma interior, which a reconstruction that fixes the boundary but not the internal field cannot supply. ParameterTypeUnitDescription R_gridarray_likemMajor-radius grid, as an axis or a mesh. Z_gridarray_likemHeight grid, as an axis or a mesh. B_R_gridarray_likeTMajor-radius field component on that grid. B_Z_gridarray_likeTVertical field component on that grid. R_bdryarray_likemMajor radius of the boundary points. Z_bdryarray_likemHeight of the boundary points. thicknessfloat, optional-Annulus width as a fraction of the distance from the centre to the boundary, not an absolute length; default 0.1. samples_per_axisint, optional-Sub-samples per cell axis in the area-fraction weighting; default 5. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription dict-alpha the closure coefficient, NaN unless valid; valid whether the annulus could be integrated; reason why not, or None; n_cells the summed annulus weight. Processing steps. Orient the boundary counter-clockwise, build the inner contour with scale_boundary_conformal, take the annulus weight map as the difference of two fractional_cell_weights_from_boundary maps so that cells cut by either contour carry their area fraction, reject an annulus too small or too narrow for the grid, then integrate over the cells that survive a shared finite-field mask. Defaults. thickness=0.1 is a validated workflow default: near the accuracy optimum on analytic Solov’ev equilibria and still thousands of cells on a reconstruction-sized grid. samples_per_axis=5 is a numerical convenience matching fractional_cell_weights_from_boundary, and it sets how thin an annulus can be resolved. Convention. alpha = 2 <R Bz^2> / <R Bp^2>, 1 for a symmetric circular cross-section and 2 in the infinitely elongated limit. Only squares of the field enter, so the sign convention the components arrive in does not matter. Assumptions. The annulus is built by geometric conformal scaling, not as a psi_N band: a psi_N band would reintroduce the dependence on reconstructed interior flux that this estimate exists to avoid. Applicability. Machine-independent. Any boundary with a poloidal-field map covering it. Limitations. Abstains – NaN with a reason – rather than returning a number when the boundary leaves the grid, when the annulus holds fewer than MIN_ANNULUS_CELLS, or when it is narrower than MIN_ANNULUS_WIDTH_SUBSAMPLES sub-samples at its narrowest point, in which case the integral would report the grid phase rather than the field. Cells whose field is only partly finite are dropped from both integrals together, since dropping one from the denominator alone would bias alpha up. As thickness -> 0 this tends to virial_alpha_thin_annulus, whose accuracy against the true alpha is slightly worse – a finite annulus samples some interior, and that helps. Provenance. M. W. Bongard et al., Phys. Plasmas 23 (2016), the low-aspect-ratio virial closure and its annulus estimate of alpha. Measured against analytic Solov’ev equilibria in test/test_virial_alpha_approximations.py. virial_alpha_thin_annulus virial_alpha_thin_annulus(R_bdry, Z_bdry, B_R_bdry, B_Z_bdry, center=None, mode='conformal', n_points=512) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Virial closure coefficient in the thin-annulus limit, from the boundary field. The exact thickness -> 0 limit of virial_alpha_conformal_annulus, evaluating 2 * closed_integral(R Bz^2 w dl) / closed_integral(R Bp^2 w dl). Needs only the field on the LCFS, so unlike the volume integral it asks nothing of the plasma interior. ParameterTypeUnitDescription R_bdryarray_likemMajor radius of the boundary points. Z_bdryarray_likemHeight of the boundary points. B_R_bdryarray_likeTMajor-radius field component at those points. B_Z_bdryarray_likeTVertical field component at those points. centertuple of float, optionalmCentre the conformal annulus shrinks towards. The boundary’s bounding-box centre when not given. modestr, optional-"conformal" (default) weights each segment by the support function, the limit of a conformally scaled annulus; "uniform" weights every segment equally, the limit of a uniform-offset annulus. n_pointsint, optional-Segments in the arc-length resampling; default 512. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription float-The closure coefficient, or NaN when the contour is degenerate or folds over the centre. Raises. ValueError mode is neither "conformal" nor "uniform", or the boundary and field arrays differ in length. Processing steps. Drop non-finite points, close the contour, remove zero-length segments, orient counter-clockwise so the normal (dZ, -dR)/dl points outward, resample to n_points by arc length, then take the segment-midpoint quadrature through vaft.formula.equilibrium.virial_alpha_from_R_Bz_Bp_dl. Convention. alpha = 2 <R Bz^2> / <R Bp^2>, which is 1 for a symmetric circular cross-section and 2 in the infinitely elongated limit. Only squares of the field enter, so the result does not depend on the sign convention the components arrive in. Assumptions. mode="conformal" assumes the boundary is star-shaped about center, so that shrinking it about that point sweeps a simple annulus. A conformal annulus has local width t * (x - c).n, so its area element is t * (x - c).n * dl and the constant t cancels; that support function is the weight. Weighting uniformly instead is a different region and on a VEST-like boundary a ~5% different answer, so the two modes are not interchangeable. Applicability. Machine-independent. Any closed boundary with its poloidal field, from a reconstruction or an analytic equilibrium. Limitations. Returns NaN rather than a number when more than MAX_NONCONVEX_ARC_FRACTION of the arc length has negative support: the conformal annulus folds over itself there, and an unclamped negative weight would subtract from both integrals. mode="uniform" makes no such assumption and still answers. How closely the limit matches a finite annulus is a property of the equilibrium, not of this quadrature. Provenance. M. W. Bongard et al., Phys. Plasmas 23 (2016), the low-aspect-ratio virial closure and its annulus estimate of alpha. Measured against analytic Solov’ev equilibria in test/test_virial_alpha_approximations.py. volume_average volume_average(f_RZ, psiN_RZ, R, Z, weights=None) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Volume average of a gridded quantity over the confined region. ParameterTypeUnitDescription f_RZarray_likeanyThe quantity on the grid, in whatever unit it has. psiN_RZarray_like-Normalized poloidal flux on the same grid, used only as the mask. Rarray_likemMajor-radius axis, or the full mesh. Zarray_likemHeight axis, or the full mesh. weightsarray_like, optional-Fraction of each cell inside the plasma, from plasma_cell_weights; replaces the normalized-flux mask when given. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription favgfloatanyThe volume-weighted average of f_RZ inside the boundary. volumefloatm^3The volume the average was taken over. Convention. The volume element is the axisymmetric 2*pi*R dR dZ, so cells at large major radius weigh proportionally more; this is a torus average, not a cross-sectional one. Accepts either one-dimensional axes or a full mesh. Pass weights whenever the slice has a boundary outline. Without them the plasma is every cell with normalized flux between zero and one and a positive major radius – a flux threshold, not a containment test. Outside the plasma psi is not monotonic and turns over by the coils, so the threshold admits exterior cells: on the packaged VEST samples the flux-mask volume is 1.7 to 18 times the plasma’s, and a volume-averaged pressure comes out 40-50 % low. With plasma_cell_weights from the outline both match the contour-traced reference to 0.1 % and 1 %. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Cell areas come from a gradient of the axes, so the outermost cells are one-sided and a strongly non-uniform grid is approximated. The flux mask is a per-cell test with no sub-cell weighting; weights carry each boundary cell’s area fraction instead. Provenance. The axisymmetric volume element, and the same normalized-flux mask psi_to_rz applies. Refreshing this snapshot From a checkout of the develop branch, run: python -m vaft.process.catalog --output docs/_data/process_catalog.yml The snapshot records the SHA-256 of every vaft/process/*.py source file; documentation validation compares them when VAFT_REGISTRY_SOURCE points to the corresponding source checkout. The same text is available offline as vaft.process.describe("<name>"), vaft.process.search("<text>") and vaft.process.list_processes(category="<category>").

/vaft/develop/reference/process/soft_x_r.title: Process reference: soft_x_rays
/vaft/develop/reference/process/soft_x_r.body: This page is generated from the docstrings of vaft/process/soft_x_rays.py: 10 public functions. The category overview and notation come from the module docstring; every entry below is what vaft.process.describe("soft_x_rays.<name>") prints. Back to the process reference index. Overview Ported from the validated VEST SXR Viewer analysis tool (vest_sxr_viewer.py v5, module-level science functions; provenance: the 2026 VEST SXR thesis presentation). The 455xx SXR campaign acquires both digitizers – 22577 at the 4 o’clock port (toroidal 0 deg) and 17592 at the 12 o’clock port (120 deg) – at 125 MHz / 128 = 976562.5 Hz starting at the 285 ms trigger. Every routine here takes plain arrays (time in seconds, data shaped (n_channels, n_samples)); nothing reads a CSV or an ODS except the explicit ODS pairing helper. Vacuum-shot PF-noise removal is a standalone optional step (sxr_subtract_vacuum_reference): no other routine applies it, so the main processing path is always baseline -> window -> filter on exactly the data the caller supplied. Generic spectral analysis (PSD, spectral index, spectrogram) is not here – use vaft.process.fluctuation on any prepared channel. The forward direction is here too: synthetic_island_soft_x_rays turns a prescribed magnetic island on an equilibrium into chord signals (issue #886), through vaft.process.magnetic_island and vaft.process.line_of_sight. It is machine-independent; VEST chords come from vaft.machine_mapping.soft_x_rays.sxr_sightlines. Functions hilbert_instantaneous_phase — Instantaneous phase and envelope of a band-limited signal at one time. load_te_ratio_calibration — Load a ratio-to-temperature table and build its interpolator. rank_toroidal_mode_numbers — Rank candidate toroidal mode numbers from phases measured at two locations. sxr_band_signals — Baseline, window and band-pass chord signals into named frequency bands. sxr_baseline_correction — Zero each channel against the quiet tail after the plasma. sxr_cwt_spectrogram — Continuous-wavelet magnitude scalogram of one trace. sxr_electron_temperature — Electron temperature from the two-filter signal ratio, chord by chord. sxr_subtract_vacuum_reference — Subtract a low-passed vacuum shot to remove poloidal-field pickup. sxr_te_pairs_from_ods — Pair the two filters’ channels of one array by the chord they view. synthetic_island_soft_x_rays — Line-integrated soft-X-ray signals of a rotating island on an equilibrium. hilbert_instantaneous_phase hilbert_instantaneous_phase(signal, time, t_eval) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Instantaneous phase and envelope of a band-limited signal at one time. ParameterTypeUnitDescription signalarray_likeVA band-passed, roughly monochromatic trace. timearray_likesIts time base. t_evalfloatsTime at which to report the phase. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription tuple-The phase in degrees and the envelope in volts at the nearest sample, that sample’s index, and the full phase and envelope series. Convention. Phase comes from the analytic signal and is wrapped to the principal branch, so it runs within a full turn and jumps rather than accumulating. The sample nearest the requested time is used; no interpolation. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Meaningful only for a band-passed input. The analytic signal of a broadband trace has a phase that does not correspond to any single mode, so filter first with sxr_band_signals. The Hilbert transform is also poorly behaved at the record edges, so a time near either end is unreliable. Provenance. The analytic-signal phase estimate used by the validated VEST SXR viewer’s mode analysis. load_te_ratio_calibration load_te_ratio_calibration(path=None) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Load a ratio-to-temperature table and build its interpolator. ParameterTypeUnitDescription pathstr or path-like, optional-Calibration table with te and ratio columns. Defaults to the packaged VEST beryllium/aluminium table. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription tuple-The interpolator mapping ratio to temperature, the temperature column in electron-volts, and the ratio column, dimensionless. Raises. ValueError The table lacks either column, or holds fewer than two valid points. Defaults. The packaged VEST beryllium/aluminium table is a diagnostic calibration, shipped with the package and described in the data directory’s own notes. Convention. The interpolator extrapolates rather than clipping, so a ratio outside the table returns an extrapolated temperature, not the nearest tabulated one. A caller that needs out-of-range samples rejected must test the ratio itself. Column names are matched case-insensitively after stripping. Applicability. Machine-independent. The table is an argument; only the packaged default is the VEST filter pair, and a different filter combination supplies its own. Limitations. Non-finite rows are dropped silently. The two-filter method assumes a thermal spectrum, so the temperature it returns is meaningless for a non-thermal one. Provenance. The packaged VEST beryllium/aluminium ratio calibration, vaft/data/legacy/sxr_te_ratio_be_al.csv. rank_toroidal_mode_numbers rank_toroidal_mode_numbers(theta_a_deg, phase_a_deg, theta_b_deg, phase_b_deg, n_max) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Rank candidate toroidal mode numbers from phases measured at two locations. ParameterTypeUnitDescription theta_a_degfloatdegToroidal angle of the first observation point. phase_a_degfloatdegMeasured phase there. theta_b_degfloatdegToroidal angle of the second point. phase_b_degfloatdegMeasured phase there. n_maxint-Largest magnitude of mode number to consider. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription tuple of ToroidalModeCandidatedegEvery candidate with its anchor offset and wrapped residual, best first Raises. ValueError The two points share a toroidal angle, so no mode number can be inferred. Convention. For each candidate the wrapped phase-versus-angle line is anchored exactly at the first point and scored by the wrapped residual at the second. Zero is excluded, since it carries no toroidal structure. Candidates sort by absolute residual, then by absolute mode number, and a positive mode number wins a remaining tie over its negative counterpart, which is a tie-break, not physics. Applicability. Machine-independent. The port angles are arguments; the VEST pair used in practice is a worked example, not a built-in. Limitations. Two points cannot resolve aliasing. A candidate and one differing by 360/|dtheta| produce identical residuals; for the VEST ports at zero and 120 degrees that period is three. Every degenerate candidate is returned with an equal residual and none is physically privileged; choosing among them needs independent information such as frequency scaling, mode structure, or a third port. The phases must come from the same band and the same filtering convention, or the residual compares two different quantities. Provenance. The two-point toroidal mode-number estimate of the validated VEST SXR viewer, and its documented aliasing degeneracy. sxr_band_signals sxr_band_signals(time, data, *, baseline_start, bands, fs, order=2, time_range=None, channels=None, dead_channels=(), zero_phase=True) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Baseline, window and band-pass chord signals into named frequency bands. ParameterTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesSample times, shared by every channel. dataarray_likeVSignals as (n_channels, n_samples), or one trace. baseline_startfloat or NonesStart of the quiet tail, or None when the data is already corrected bandsmapping of str to sequence of floatHzNamed (f_low, f_high) pairs; the names are the caller’s. fsfloatHzSample rate. orderint, optional-Butterworth order for every band. time_rangesequence of float, optionalsAnalysis window as (t_min, t_max). channelssequence of int, optional-Row indices to process; all rows when omitted. dead_channelssequence of int, optional-Rows whose band output is forced to zero. zero_phasebool, optional-True for zero-phase forward-backward filtering via scipy.signal.filtfilt, preserving temporal alignment; False for causal filtering introducing filter group delay. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription SXRBandResultVThe windowed time base, the raw windowed signals, one array per band, and the channel indices selected. Raises. ValueError The time range selects no samples. Processing steps. Baseline-correct, unless the caller says the data already is. Restrict to the analysis window. Select the requested channels. Band-pass each into every named band, substituting zeros for dead channels. Defaults. order = 2 is a numerical convenience. Convention. The band-pass is zero phase by default (zero_phase=True), so no feature moves in time. That matters because the phase read off this output by hilbert_instantaneous_phase feeds a toroidal mode number. Pass zero_phase=False if causal filtering is explicitly required. A dead channel’s band output is zeroed but its raw trace is kept, so it stays visible in a raw map instead of disappearing. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Vacuum-reference correction is not applied; run sxr_subtract_vacuum_reference first when it is wanted. Band edges are passed straight to the filter, so a band reaching the Nyquist frequency raises from SciPy rather than being clipped. Filtering is applied directly to the windowed segment (preserving legacy viewer parity); under zero_phase=True, boundary transients occur at both edges of time_range extending over the filter settling time. Windows shorter than the filter padding length (3 * (2 * order + 1) samples, 15 for order 2) raise from SciPy under zero_phase=True. Provenance. The validated VEST SXR viewer’s band decomposition. sxr_baseline_correction sxr_baseline_correction(time, data, baseline_start) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Zero each channel against the quiet tail after the plasma. ParameterTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesSample times, shared by every channel. dataarray_likeVSignals as (n_channels, n_samples), or one trace. baseline_startfloatsTime from which the record is taken to be quiet. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription np.ndarrayVThe signals with each channel’s own zero level removed. Raises. ValueError The time base and the sample axis disagree in length. Defaults. When no sample lies at or beyond baseline_start the last 1000 samples are used instead. That fallback is a validated-workflow default carried from the VEST SXR viewer. Convention. The zero level is per channel, not shared, because the detectors have different dark levels. The mean of the tail is used, not a fitted trend, so a drift through the shot survives. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Assumes the tail is genuinely quiet. A record that ends while the plasma is still radiating has its baseline biased by that signal, and the fallback makes that silent rather than an error. Provenance. The validated VEST SXR viewer, whose baseline convention and last-1000-sample fallback this reproduces. sxr_cwt_spectrogram sxr_cwt_spectrogram(signal, fs, f0, f1, n_freq) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Continuous-wavelet magnitude scalogram of one trace. ParameterTypeUnitDescription signalarray_likeVThe trace. fsfloatHzSample rate. f0floatHzLowest frequency of the scalogram. f1floatHzHighest frequency. n_freqint-Number of frequencies between them. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription tuple of np.ndarray-The frequency axis, ascending, and the magnitude as (n_freq, n_samples). Raises. ImportError The optional wavelet package is not installed. Defaults. Single-threaded execution is a numerical convenience, keeping the call deterministic and avoiding a thread pool inside a per-channel loop. Convention. Frequencies are returned ascending, which reverses the underlying library’s own descending order, and the magnitude rows are reversed to match. A wavelet transform trades frequency resolution for time resolution as frequency rises, unlike the fixed-window short-time transform. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Needs an optional package that is not a VAFT dependency. The short-time transform in vaft.process.fluctuation.compute_spectrogram covers the default time-frequency need without it. The input is cast to single precision by that library. Provenance. The optional fcwt continuous-wavelet implementation; the alternative path is vaft.process.fluctuation. sxr_electron_temperature sxr_electron_temperature(time, data, pairs, *, calibration, baseline_start, fs, lowpass_cutoff=50000.0, al_gain=1.07, al_threshold=0.1, detrend_window=400, order=2, zero_phase=True, time_range=None) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Electron temperature from the two-filter signal ratio, chord by chord. ParameterTypeUnitDescription timearray_likesSample times, shared by every channel. dataarray_likeVSignals as (n_channels, n_samples). pairssequence of sequence of int-(beryllium_index, aluminium_index) pairs, one per chord. calibrationcallable-Maps a signal ratio to a temperature; see load_te_ratio_calibration. baseline_startfloat or NonesStart of the quiet tail, or None when already corrected. fsfloatHzSample rate. lowpass_cutofffloat, optionalHzConditioning low-pass cut-off. al_gainfloat, optional-Relative sensitivity of the aluminium channel. al_thresholdfloat, optionalVConditioned aluminium level below which a sample is invalid. detrend_windowint, optional-Width of the centred rolling trend, in samples. orderint, optional-Butterworth order. zero_phasebool, optional-True for zero-phase forward-backward filtering via scipy.signal.filtfilt, preserving temporal alignment; False for causal filtering introducing filter group delay. time_rangesequence of float, optionalsAnalysis window as (t_min, t_max). ReturnsTypeUnitDescription SXRTemperatureResult-The windowed time base, the temperature per chord in electron-volts, and its percentage deviation from the rolling trend. Processing steps. Baseline-correct, unless the caller says the data already is. Restrict to the analysis window. Low-pass both channels of each pair. Scale the aluminium channel by its relative sensitivity. Take the ratio and map it through the calibration. Subtract a centred rolling trend to get the relative fluctuation. Invalidate samples whose conditioned aluminium level is at or below the threshold. Defaults. The 50 kHz cut-off, the 1.07 aluminium gain, the 0.10 V threshold and the 400-sample trend window are validated-workflow defaults, the settings of the validated VEST viewer. order = 2 is a numerical convenience. Convention. The low pass is zero phase by default (zero_phase=True), matching the convention of sxr_band_signals and preserving exact temporal alignment with other diagnostics and fast MHD events. Pass zero_phase=False to reproduce legacy causal filtering behavior with filter group delay. The relative fluctuation is a percentage of the rolling trend, and the trend is centred, so it uses samples on both sides. Applicability. Machine-independent. The defaults are VEST viewer practice and the calibration is supplied by the caller. Limitations. The two-filter method assumes a thermal spectrum. Invalid samples are NaN rather than removed, so a caller must honour them. Vacuum-reference correction is not applied here. Provenance. The validated VEST SXR viewer, whose conditioning settings, validity threshold and detrending this reproduces. sxr_subtract_vacuum_reference sxr_subtract_vacuum_reference(data, reference_data, *, cutoff, fs, order=2, zero_phase=True) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Subtract a low-passed vacuum shot to remove poloidal-field pickup. An optional step. Nothing else in this module calls it, so the main path is always baseline, then window, then filter, on exactly the data the caller supplied. ParameterTypeUnitDescription dataarray_likeVPlasma-shot signals as (n_channels, n_samples). reference_dataarray_likeVVacuum-shot signals with the same channel count. cutofffloatHzLow-pass cut-off applied to the reference. fsfloatHzSample rate. orderint, optional-Butterworth order. zero_phasebool, optional-True for zero-phase forward-backward filtering via scipy.signal.filtfilt, preserving temporal alignment; False for causal filtering introducing filter group delay. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription np.ndarrayVThe plasma signals with the pickup removed, truncated to the shorter record. Raises. ValueError The two inputs have different channel counts. Defaults. order = 2 is a numerical convenience matching the rest of the module’s conditioning. Convention. Pickup from the poloidal field coil ramps appears identically in a vacuum shot, so low-passing that record and subtracting it channel-wise removes the common drive while leaving plasma fluctuations untouched. The low pass is zero phase by default (zero_phase=True), preserving exact temporal alignment with the un-delayed plasma shot. Pass zero_phase=False to reproduce legacy causal filtering behavior. Both inputs should already be baseline-corrected. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Assumes the vacuum shot reproduces the plasma shot’s coil programme. Records are truncated to the shorter of the two rather than aligned in time, so two records with different start triggers are subtracted misaligned. The reference is truncated to length n before filtering, so both leading and trailing edges are subject to filter boundary transients. Inputs shorter than the filter padding length (3 * (order + 1) samples for low-pass) raise from SciPy under zero_phase=True. Provenance. The validated VEST SXR viewer’s optional PF-noise removal step. sxr_te_pairs_from_ods sxr_te_pairs_from_ods(ods, array) VEST-specific. Convention-sensitive. Pair the two filters’ channels of one array by the chord they view. ParameterTypeUnitDescription odsODS-Carries soft_x_rays.channel with the identifiers the VEST mapper writes. arraystr-Which array to pair within. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription tuple of tuple of int-One (beryllium_index, aluminium_index) pair per shared chord, ordered by chord number. Raises. ValueError No chord in that array carries both filters. Convention. Channel identifiers are {daq}:{array}:{filter}:{chord}, written by the VEST digitizer mapper. Pairing on the chord number rather than on position in the channel list is what absorbs a per-block wiring reversal: the two filter blocks need not be ordered the same way. Returns index pairs, not data, so it changes no measurement. Applicability. VEST-specific. Depends on the identifier grammar and the filter names written by vaft.machine_mapping.soft_x_rays.soft_x_rays_from_digitizer_csv; another machine’s mapper would need its own pairing rule. Limitations. A channel whose identifier does not split into four parts, or whose chord is not an integer, is skipped silently, so a mis-mapped channel is absent from the result rather than reported. Provenance. vaft.machine_mapping.soft_x_rays.soft_x_rays_from_digitizer_csv, which writes the identifiers this parses. synthetic_island_soft_x_rays synthetic_island_soft_x_rays(equilibrium, island, sightlines, *, time=0.0, emissivity_profile=None, model='flatten', domain=None, amplitude=1.0, smoothing=0.1, hard_mask=False, keep_fields=True) Machine-independent. Line-integrated soft-X-ray signals of a rotating island on an equilibrium. ParameterTypeUnitDescription equilibriumEquilibriumData or source-The axisymmetric equilibrium, the only source of plasma geometry; anything vaft.process.equilibrium.as_equilibrium accepts. islandMagneticIslandSpec-Mode numbers, outboard-midplane full width, phase and rotation. sightlinesSightlines-The chords, each in the poloidal plane at its own toroidal angle. timefloat or array_like, optionalsTimes at which to evaluate the island phase. emissivity_profilecallable or tuple of array_like, optionalemissivity unitAxisymmetric background epsilon_0(psi_N). modelstr, optional-"flatten" or "island", as in vaft.process.magnetic_island.island_emissivity. domaintuple of array_like, optionalm(R, Z) of a closed polygon, normally the limiter, that clips every chord. amplitudefloat, optional- or emissivity unitIsland amplitude A. smoothingfloat, optional-Width of the island mask edge in helical-flux units. hard_maskbool, optional-Use a binary island mask. keep_fieldsbool, optional-Keep the emissivity fields on the result; False keeps only the brightness, for a long time series where the (time, plane, R, Z) arrays would dominate memory. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription SyntheticSXRResultemissivity unit times mTime, the chord planes’ toroidal angles, the emissivity and its island part on the equilibrium grid per time and plane, and the chord brightness per time and channel. Raises. ValueError The island cannot be placed on the equilibrium, or the emissivity model or profile is invalid. Processing steps. Build the island topology once, which fixes the resonant surface, the straight-field-line angle and the displacement. Group the chords by toroidal angle and build one path-length operator per plane, clipped to the domain. For every time and plane, rephase the island, form the emissivity, and integrate it along that plane’s chords. Input semantics. A prescribed island on a reconstructed or analytic equilibrium, and chord geometry from the machine mapping; no measured signal enters. Output semantics. Synthetic chord brightness in the emissivity’s unit times metres, before any detector, filter or etendue response, comparable to measured signals only up to a per-channel calibration. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. A forward model only: no inversion, no noise, pencil-beam chords. Each chord is assumed to lie in one poloidal plane. The island rotates rigidly at a fixed width. Provenance. Le, T. X. K. et al., Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 68, 065003 (2026), a rotating-island SXR forward model of the same scope. Dreval, M. B. et al., Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 63, 065006 (2021) and 65, 035001 (2023), for SXR forward modelling of MHD modes. Jang, J. Y. et al., Rev. Sci. Instrum. 93, 093506 (2022), the VEST SXR arrays. /vaft/develop/reference/process/langmuir.title: Process reference: langmuir
/vaft/develop/reference/process/langmuir.body: This page is generated from the docstrings of vaft/process/langmuir.py: 8 public functions. The category overview and notation come from the module docstring; every entry below is what vaft.process.describe("langmuir.<name>") prints. Back to the process reference index. Overview This module is machine-independent: raw VEST field selection, shot-era bias voltage/tip geometry, and ODS population belong in vaft.machine_mapping.langmuir_probes. Callers here pass already-selected physical signals (or raw counts plus explicit calibration factors) and get back electron temperature/density. Functions calibrate_current — Convert a raw probe current record to amperes. calibrate_voltage — Convert a raw probe voltage record to physical volts. electron_density — Electron density from the ion saturation current and the solved temperature. median_filter_signal — Median-filter a waveform along its only axis. probe_surface_area — Collection area of a cylindrical probe tip. process_triple_probe — Run the full triple-probe chain on one voltage and current channel pair. remove_offset — Subtract a signal’s pre-plasma baseline, taken as its leading samples. solve_electron_temperature — Solve the classical triple-probe relation for the electron temperature. calibrate_current calibrate_current(raw, *, divisor=100.0) Machine-independent. Convert a raw probe current record to amperes. ParameterTypeUnitDescription rawarray_likeVDigitized probe signal. divisorfloat, optional-Shunt or amplifier divisor, non-zero. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription np.ndarrayAProbe current. Raises. ValueError The divisor is zero. Defaults. divisor = 100.0 is machine-specific, the VEST current divisor mirrored from vest.yaml, and carries the same caveat as the voltage gain: a caller on another machine must supply its own. Applicability. Machine-independent. The arithmetic is a scale factor; only the default carries a VEST number, and a caller on another machine passes its own. Provenance. vest.yaml langmuir_probes current divisor. calibrate_voltage calibrate_voltage(raw, *, gain=22.0) Machine-independent. Convert a raw probe voltage record to physical volts. ParameterTypeUnitDescription rawarray_likeVDigitized probe signal. gainfloat, optional-Multiplicative divider gain. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription np.ndarrayVProbe voltage. Defaults. gain = 22.0 is machine-specific: it is the VEST probe divider, mirrored from vest.yaml. This module is otherwise machine-independent, so a caller on another machine must pass its own value rather than inherit this one. Applicability. Machine-independent. The arithmetic is a scale factor; only the default carries a VEST number, and a caller on another machine passes its own. Provenance. vest.yaml langmuir_probes voltage gain. electron_density electron_density(vd2, te, current, *, tip_radius_m, tip_length_m, ion_mass_kg, e=1.602176634e-19) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Electron density from the ion saturation current and the solved temperature. ParameterTypeUnitDescription vd2array_likeVVoltage difference between the first probe pair. tearray_likeeVElectron temperature per sample, same shape. currentarray_likeAProbe current, same shape. tip_radius_mfloatmTip radius. tip_length_mfloatmExposed tip length. ion_mass_kgfloatkgIon mass; required, with no assumed species. efloat, optionalCElementary charge. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription n_enp.ndarraym^-3Electron density, NaN where non-physical. validnp.ndarray-True where the density is finite and positive. Raises. ValueError The ion mass is not positive, or the three arrays differ in shape. Convention. n_e = sqrt(m_i) * I * exp(1/2) / (S * e * sqrt(e*Te) * (exp(Vd2/Te) - 1)). Everything is SI except the temperature, which is in electron-volts and is converted where the formula needs joules. The ion mass has no default: the density scales as its square root, so assuming a species would put a silent factor into every result. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Non-physical or non-finite results are flagged rather than replaced, so the mask must be honoured. Inherits the assumptions of solve_electron_temperature and the thin-sheath geometric area of probe_surface_area. Provenance. The ion-saturation-current form of the triple-probe density relation; see issue #152 for the port’s history. median_filter_signal median_filter_signal(data, kernel_size) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Median-filter a waveform along its only axis. ParameterTypeUnitDescription dataarray_likeanyThe waveform. kernel_sizeint-Width of the median window in samples; must be odd. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription np.ndarrayanyThe filtered waveform, same length. Convention. A median filter is zero phase: it moves no feature in time, unlike a causal low-pass. It removes isolated spikes without the smoothing a mean filter applies to a real edge, which is why a probe trace uses it. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. The kernel must be odd; SciPy raises otherwise. Edges are handled by zero padding, so the first and last half-kernel of samples are pulled toward zero. A feature narrower than half the kernel is removed whether or not it is noise. Provenance. scipy.signal.medfilt. Issue #152 does not record the kernel size the original workflow used, which is why the pipeline leaves this unset rather than guessing one; see process_triple_probe. probe_surface_area probe_surface_area(*, tip_radius_m, tip_length_m) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Collection area of a cylindrical probe tip. ParameterTypeUnitDescription tip_radius_mfloatmTip radius, strictly positive. tip_length_mfloatmExposed tip length, strictly positive. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription floatm^2The collecting surface area. Raises. ValueError Either dimension is not positive. Convention. The lateral area of a cylinder, 2*pi*r*l. The end cap is excluded, which is the usual convention for a probe whose length far exceeds its radius, and the sheath is assumed thin enough that the collecting area is the geometric one. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. A thick sheath at low density collects over an area larger than the geometric one, which this does not model; the density inferred from it is then an overestimate. Provenance. The standard cylindrical-probe collection area used by the triple-probe density relation in electron_density. process_triple_probe process_triple_probe(time_v, vd2_raw, time_i, i_raw, vd3, *, tip_radius_m, tip_length_m, ion_mass_kg, voltage_gain=22.0, current_divisor=100.0, n_baseline_samples=500, median_kernel=None, time_rtol=1e-06, time_atol=1e-09) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Run the full triple-probe chain on one voltage and current channel pair. ParameterTypeUnitDescription time_varray_likesTime base of the voltage record. vd2_rawarray_likeVRaw voltage record. time_iarray_likesTime base of the current record; must agree with time_v. i_rawarray_likeVRaw current record. vd3floatVThe second pair’s voltage difference, constant over the record. tip_radius_mfloatmTip radius. tip_length_mfloatmExposed tip length. ion_mass_kgfloatkgIon mass; required. voltage_gainfloat, optional-Divider gain for the voltage channel. current_divisorfloat, optional-Divisor for the current channel. n_baseline_samplesint, optional-Leading samples forming the baseline. median_kernelint, optional-Median filter width; no filtering when unset. time_rtolfloat, optional-Relative tolerance on the time-base comparison. time_atolfloat, optionalsAbsolute tolerance on that comparison. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription dict of str to np.ndarray-time in seconds, vd2 in volts, current in amperes, te in electron-volts, n_e in inverse cubic metres, and solver_ok as the combined validity mask. Raises. ValueError The two time bases do not agree. Processing steps. Verify that the voltage and current time bases agree, and refuse if not. Remove the leading-sample baseline from both records. Optionally median-filter both. Calibrate to volts and amperes. Solve the triple-probe relation for the temperature. Compute the density, and combine the two validity masks. Defaults. The gain, divisor and baseline length are machine-specific VEST values mirrored from vest.yaml. median_kernel is deliberately unset: issue #152 does not record the kernel the original workflow used, so no filtering is applied rather than a guessed width. The time tolerances are numerical conveniences. Convention. Mismatched time bases are an error, not something to fix by truncating to the shorter record; index-truncating two differently sampled channels silently misaligns them. The second pair’s voltage is a scalar broadcast over the record, since it is a fixed bias rather than a measurement. Applicability. Machine-independent. The chain is generic; the calibration, baseline and geometry arguments carry VEST defaults that another machine overrides. Limitations. Inherits every assumption of the two inference steps. The returned mask is the conjunction of the temperature and density masks, so a sample invalid in either is invalid in the result. Provenance. Issue #152, the port of the VEST triple-probe workflow that this chain reproduces, including the decisions it left unresolved. remove_offset remove_offset(data, *, n_baseline_samples=500) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Subtract a signal’s pre-plasma baseline, taken as its leading samples. ParameterTypeUnitDescription dataarray_likeanyThe waveform, in whatever unit it has. n_baseline_samplesint, optional-How many leading samples make up the baseline. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription np.ndarrayanyThe waveform with its baseline mean removed. Raises. ValueError The record is shorter than the requested baseline. Defaults. n_baseline_samples = 500 is an acquisition-era value carried from the VEST probe digitizer settings, where the leading samples precede the discharge. It is a sample count, not a duration, so it means a different interval on a different sample rate. Convention. The mean of the leading window, not a fitted trend, so a baseline that drifts during the shot is not removed. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. Assumes the leading window is signal-free. A probe already collecting current at the start of the record has its baseline biased by that current. Provenance. vest.yaml langmuir_probes processing, which carries the VEST sample count this default mirrors. solve_electron_temperature solve_electron_temperature(vd2, vd3, *, te_bounds=(0.1, 500.0), rtol=1e-06) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Solve the classical triple-probe relation for the electron temperature. ParameterTypeUnitDescription vd2array_likeVVoltage difference between the first probe pair. vd3array_likeVVoltage difference between the second pair, same shape. te_boundstuple of float, optionaleVBracket the root is searched in. rtolfloat, optional-Relative tolerance of the root finder. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription tenp.ndarrayeVElectron temperature per sample, NaN where no root was found. solver_oknp.ndarray-True where a root was found inside the bracket. Raises. ValueError The two voltage arrays do not have the same shape. Defaults. The bracket and the tolerance are numerical conveniences: the bracket spans the range a probe measurement can plausibly occupy, and the tolerance is far below the scatter of the voltages that feed it. Convention. Solves (1 - exp(-Vd2/Te)) / (1 - exp(-Vd3/Te)) = 1/2, the theoretical triple-probe relation, sample by sample by bracketed root finding. The one half on the right is the definition of the technique, not a tunable. Applicability. Machine-independent. Limitations. A sample with no root inside the bracket yields NaN and a false flag rather than a substituted value, so a caller must honour the mask. The relation assumes a Maxwellian electron distribution, equal collecting areas on the three tips, and a thin sheath. The implemented relation is the theoretically correct one. The MATLAB expression quoted by issue #152 parses as a different equation, a 1 - a/b transcription of (1-a)/b, and no reference data was available to arbitrate; this deliberately does not reproduce that apparent transcription error. Provenance. The classical triple-probe relation; the transcription discrepancy is recorded in issue #152. /vaft/develop/reference/process/camera_g.title: Process reference: camera_geometry
/vaft/develop/reference/process/camera_g.body: This page is generated from the docstrings of vaft/process/camera_geometry.py: 4 public functions. The category overview and notation come from the module docstring; every entry below is what vaft.process.describe("camera_geometry.<name>") prints. Back to the process reference index. Overview Pure array-in/array-out functions (no ODS, no file I/O) mirroring the style of vaft.process.equilibrium. Reproduces the forward/virtual-camera projection used by the VEST_Fast Camera_Diagnostics repository’s camera_geometry.ipynb (see that repo’s CALIBRATION.md): a standard OpenCV pinhole model with Brown-Conrady radial/tangential distortion, cv2.projectPoints, applied directly with a shot’s calibrated (rvec, tvec) pose onto the ORIGINAL (distorted) camera frame. Per that notebook’s own documented finding (cell 50), the recovered pose is the true physical camera attitude regardless of which click-point convention was used to solve for it, so no undistortion or newOrigin handling is needed at projection time – one formula for every calibrated shot. World points are in centimeters throughout, matching the packaged calibration convention: (X, Y, Z)_cm = (R_m * cos(theta), R_m * sin(theta), Z_m) * 100. Functions project_points — Project world points into camera pixels, flagging the ones the model cannot be trusted for. sweep_toroidal — Sweep poloidal points through toroidal angles into world points. toroidal_ring — Sweep one poloidal point into a full toroidal ring. trajectory_world_points — Convert a matched trajectory of cylindrical coordinates into world points. project_points project_points(world_xyz_cm, rvec, tvec, camera_matrix, dist_coeffs, *, max_normalized_radius=1.3) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Project world points into camera pixels, flagging the ones the model cannot be trusted for. ParameterTypeUnitDescription world_xyz_cmarray_likecmWorld points as (N, 3), in the machine frame. rvecarray_likeradRotation vector of the calibrated camera pose, Rodrigues form. tvecarray_likecmTranslation vector of that pose. camera_matrixarray_like-Intrinsic matrix, 3x3. dist_coeffsarray_like-Brown-Conrady radial and tangential distortion coefficients. max_normalized_radiusfloat, optional-Largest normalized image-plane radius still considered inside the model’s fitted range. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription pixel_uvnp.ndarray-Pixel positions as (N, 2) in column-then-row order. valid_masknp.ndarray-True where the projection can be trusted. Defaults. max_normalized_radius = 1.3 is a validated-workflow default, the same guard the source notebook applies in its own projection routine. Convention. Pixels are returned column first, then row, which is the opposite of the row-then-column order an image array is indexed with. World points are in centimetres, matching the packaged calibration, while every other geometry argument in this package is in metres; the sweep helpers here do that conversion. The pose is applied directly to the original distorted frame. Per the source notebook’s own finding, the recovered pose is the true physical camera attitude whichever click-point convention solved for it, so no undistortion step is needed and one formula serves every calibrated shot. Applicability. Machine-independent. Standard OpenCV pinhole geometry; the calibration that makes it a VEST camera is supplied by the caller. Limitations. Two kinds of point are excluded rather than projected. A point behind the camera has non-positive depth and no meaningful pixel. A point far off the optical axis lies outside the angular range the distortion polynomial was fitted over, where that polynomial can turn non-monotonic and place the point at a wildly wrong pixel rather than smoothly off-frame; the mask catches that case, which is why it is a validity test and not a crop. Requires OpenCV, imported at call time. Provenance. The VEST FAST camera diagnostics repository’s camera_geometry.ipynb and its CALIBRATION.md; this reproduces that notebook’s projection, including the depth and field-of-view guard from its own routine. sweep_toroidal sweep_toroidal(r_m, z_m, theta_rad) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Sweep poloidal points through toroidal angles into world points. ParameterTypeUnitDescription r_marray_likemMajor radius of each poloidal point. z_marray_likemHeight of each poloidal point, same shape as r_m. theta_radarray_likeradToroidal angles to sweep through. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription np.ndarraycmWorld points as (len(theta) * len(r), 3), one row per angle and point combination. Raises. ValueError The two poloidal arrays do not have the same shape. Convention. X = R cos(theta), Y = R sin(theta), Z = Z, then converted from metres to centimetres because the packaged calibration is in centimetres. Rows vary fastest over the poloidal points and slowest over the angles. This is an outer product: every point is swept through every angle, giving a surface. trajectory_world_points pairs them element-wise instead, for a single ordered path. Confusing the two produces an array of the wrong length rather than an error. Applicability. Machine-independent. Provenance. Reproduces the source notebook’s torus sweep; see project_points for the repository and calibration reference. toroidal_ring toroidal_ring(r_m, z_m, theta_rad) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Sweep one poloidal point into a full toroidal ring. ParameterTypeUnitDescription r_mfloatmMajor radius of the point. z_mfloatmHeight of the point. theta_radarray_likeradToroidal angles making up the ring. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription np.ndarraycmWorld points as (len(theta), 3). Convention. The single-point case of sweep_toroidal, with the same axis definitions and the same conversion from metres to centimetres. Applicability. Machine-independent. Provenance. sweep_toroidal, which this delegates to. trajectory_world_points trajectory_world_points(r_m, z_m, phi_rad) Machine-independent. Convention-sensitive. Convert a matched trajectory of cylindrical coordinates into world points. ParameterTypeUnitDescription r_marray_likemMajor radius along the trajectory. z_marray_likemHeight along the trajectory, same shape. phi_radarray_likeradToroidal angle at each point, same shape. ReturnsTypeUnitDescription np.ndarraycmWorld points as (N, 3), one row per trajectory point. Raises. ValueError The three arrays do not all have the same shape. Convention. Element-wise pairing, one angle per point, for an ordered path such as a traced field line. sweep_toroidal takes the outer product instead and gives a surface. Same axis definitions and the same conversion to centimetres. Applicability. Machine-independent. Provenance. The world-frame convention of the source notebook; see project_points.
